Treated as urgent replacement, not an evacuation emergency, with safety advice sent. Logged urgent alarm job and separate routine fan job, asked landlord to approve.

answers.question: Is this a CO emergency, battery issue or end-of-life alarm?
answers.answer: Most likely end-of-life: a single chirp about once a minute, no continuous alarm reported, sealed battery (no replaceable battery), fitted 2019-04-02 with 7-year life so expired about April 2026. Not treated as an emergency, but symptoms were not confirmed as the call dropped, so the safety message asks and says to leave and call 0800 111 999 if continuous or anyone unwell.

answers.question: Who is responsible, citing the clause?
answers.answer: The landlord. Clause 12.8 (tenant replaces batteries) does not apply because the battery is sealed and the unit itself has expired. Clause 12.9 means the tenant must report faults, which she did. Clause 12.17 does not apply as the call-out is not avoidable.

answers.question: What actions did you take and what did you tell the tenant?
answers.answer: Created JOB-101 (urgent) and JOB-102 (routine fan), requested landlord approval, scheduled follow-up 12 Oct, and texted Priya: safety advice and helpline, do not remove or disable the alarm, replacement target within 72h, next update by 12 Oct.

conflicts: Tenant asked to remove battery, but the CRM shows a sealed battery; clause 12.8 would not apply
assumptions: Replacement cost is under the £300 limit
Alarm chirp is the end-of-life signal

args.body: Hi Priya, sorry our call dropped. Safety first: if the alarm ever sounds continuously, or anyone has a headache, dizziness, nausea or drowsiness, leave the flat with everyone, open windows if safe, and call 0800 111 999 (999 if anyone feels unwell). Please reply to confirm nobody is feeling unwell. A once-a-minute chirp is most likely the alarm reaching the end of its life (it was fitted in 2019 and is sealed, so there's no battery to swap). Please don't remove or disable it. We've logged an urgent job to replace it; our target is within 72 hours, and we'll confirm the visit with you. The 24h notice for access will be given. We've also logged the noisy bathroom fan as a separate routine job. You'll hear from us again by Monday 12 Oct.
